chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not write 'To the father of so-and-so' inside the letter, but write 'To the father of so-and-so' upon the address.
ai.seo_question: Where should the honorific 'Abu Fulan' be written in a letter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the formal address on the envelope and the salutation within the letter body, reflecting the scholarly tradition of precise epistolary etiquette (adab al-risalah) in early Islamic correspondence. This ruling ensures that honorifics like 'Abu Fulan' are treated as external identifiers rather than integral parts of the letter's textual content, a nuance significant in the transmission of hadith and official documents. It highlights the meticulous attention to detail in Shia jurisprudence regarding the physical and textual integrity of written communication.
